proposals.impact: converts the one session that loaded but never started
proposals.observation: The quiz data shows exactly one session loaded the intro screen in the last 48 hours. That person never pressed start. The furthest_step_distribution shows intro_load: 1 with starts: 0. One human arrived, read whatever is on the intro screen, and left. Given direct traffic was the source, this was likely someone with intent — not a cold bounce. The intro copy or CTA is not clearing the friction that stops a willing person from pressing go.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the quiz intro CTA block. The current text (below) is almost certainly generic enough that a visitor reads it and feels no particular pull. It needs to name the specific tension a 25-35 high-earner who doesn't build would recognise in their own week — the unopened bank tab, the salary that disappears without a trace — before asking them to start. One file edit: replace the CTA paragraph and button label in QuizIntro.astro.
proposals.current_text: Find out what's really driving your money decisions. This short quiz will help you understand your money personality and what to do about it.
proposals.new_text: You earn a decent salary. You know roughly what you should be doing. And yet the bank balance at the end of the month never quite adds up to the effort you put in. This takes about four minutes and tells you which pattern is running the show — and what that pattern costs you in practice.

proposals.impact: lifts open rate across the highest-performing automation by tightening subject line specificity
proposals.observation: The Money Vigilance automation has the highest open rate of the three active sequences: 66.67% on 12 sends. Money Avoidance sits at 52.63% and Money Worship at 37.5%. Vigilance is outperforming by a meaningful margin, yet the sequence has only 12 sends against Avoidance's 19. The subject lines for the lower-performing sequences are likely carrying generic framing. Lifting Money Worship's 37.5% open rate closer to the Vigilance benchmark is the fastest email win available because the audience is already subscribed — no acquisition cost.
proposals.proposal: Replace the subject line of email 1 in the Money Worship sequence. The current subject (below) is the kind of line that could come from any financial content creator. It needs to describe a specific, recognisable behaviour that a Money Worship subscriber — someone who ties self-worth to net worth — would clock as their own internal monologue, not a coaching prompt aimed at them from outside.
proposals.current_text: subject: "Your money personality results: Money Worship"
proposals.new_text: subject: "You hit the number. It didn't feel like enough. Here's why."

proposals.impact: fills the one-post queue gap created by the Daily Blog Post CI failure
proposals.observation: The Daily Blog Post CI workflow failed at 06:57 on 9 June. The content queue shows one post queued and 47 published. The failure means that queued post was not published yesterday, creating a gap in the daily cadence. The recent posts show a consistent pattern of behaviour-led titles aimed squarely at the ICP. The queued draft needs its front matter checked and a manual publish commit made today to restore the cadence before a second missed day compounds into a pattern that erodes email trust for subscribers expecting daily content.
proposals.proposal: Open the queued draft, confirm the front matter pubDate is set to today (2026-06-09 or 2026-06-10 depending on publish timing), confirm no broken MDX, and commit it directly. The CI failure likely hit a generation or linting step rather than a content problem, so a clean manual commit of a well-formed file will bypass the failed workflow and restore publication.
